records.rationale: The handler queries prisma.booking.findFirst without filtering on userId != null, and a team admin/owner or an attendee could pass the permission check even when booking.userId is null (isOrganizer would be false but not blocking). Then prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) would throw a raw Prisma P2025 error rather than a handled TRPCError, producing an unhandled 500. The schema allows null userId (the code itself guards with `booking.userId || 0`, acknowledging nullability), so the mechanism is real and introduced by this diff.

records.rationale: The diff shows `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` (addGuests.handler.ts) is not inside any try/catch, while only `sendAddGuestsEmails` is wrapped. It runs after `prisma.booking.update` creates the attendee rows, so a calendar failure leaves the DB mutated with no rollback and no emails sent. Also verifiable: `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and throws BAD_REQUEST if empty, so a retry with the same guest list dead-ends. This is a real error-handling/consistency defect in newly added code.
